records.title: Florida Certified Residential Contractor (CRC): CILB 5-C qualification and licensing routes
records.overview: Selected official DBPR and Construction Industry Licensing Board (CILB) licensing steps for Florida Certified Residential Contractors (CRC) under Florida Statutes Chapter 489 and CILB 5-C candidate requirements. Represents practical experience pathways, degree alternatives, military service options, residential trade experience areas (one/two-family and townhome structures up to three stories), electronic fingerprint screening, Pearson VUE state construction examination, financial responsibility requirements, and active-status insurance coverage. This is not a formal legal determination of eligibility; individual applications are evaluated directly by the Department.
records.review_note: Revision 1 establishes the verified CILB residential contractor licensing pathway based on F.S. § 489.111, F.A.C. Rule 61G4, and the official CILB 5-C application guide. Correctly restricts scope to residential construction not exceeding three stories, models the multi-tier education and foreman experience matrix, captures military veteran alternatives, specifies the 14-hour financial responsibility course alternative for below-660 FICO scores, and details the mandatory liability insurance condition for active practice.

children.label: Qualify with an accredited four-year engineering, architecture or building-construction degree plus one year of proven residential experience
Qualify with one year as a foreman plus at least three years of accredited college-level credits
Qualify with one year as a skilled worker, one year as a foreman and at least two years of accredited college-level credits
Qualify with two years as a skilled worker, one year as a foreman and at least one year of accredited college-level credits
Qualify with four years as a skilled worker or foreman, including at least one year as a foreman in residential construction
Veteran route: document three years of military service and one year of applicable foreman experience
Veteran route: document two years of military service, one year of foreman experience and one year of applicable worker or foreman experience
Veteran route: document one year of military service, one year of foreman experience and two years of applicable worker or foreman experience
Document experience in at least four of the residential construction experience areas listed on CILB 5-C
children.condition: Experience must be on one-family, two-family, or townhome residences not exceeding three stories in height

children.label: Submit electronic fingerprints through an FDLE-approved Livescan service vendor for background screening
children.condition: Use DBPR Construction Industry Licensing Board Originating Agency Identifier (ORI) FL920250Z

children.label: Demonstrate financial responsibility with a personal FICO credit score of 660 or higher from a Board-approved credit reporting agency
children.condition: Credit reports required for applicant and business entity

children.label: If FICO is below 660, complete a Board-approved 14-hour financial responsibility course
children.condition: Proof of course completion required with CILB 5-C application

children.label: Pass the Florida State Residential Contractor Examination administered by Pearson VUE (Business & Finance and Residential Trade Knowledge)
children.condition: Examination scores valid for four years from examination date

children.label: Submit completed Form DBPR CILB 5-C Application for Certified Residential Contractor License with state fees
children.condition: Submit with credit report, experience verification, and exam passing slips

children.label: Provide proof of public liability and property damage insurance ($100,000/$25,000) and workers' compensation coverage
children.condition: Required to obtain and maintain active license status
